title: No Presentism in Quantum Gravity
relevance: Closest prior art for linking presentism to quantum gravity. Targets Monton 2006's fixed-foliation (CMC) presentism. Classifies presentist responses to SR (Fine relativized existence, Harrington point present, Stein past-light-cone). Mentions the problem of time only in passing (p. 260) and LQG time evaporation (p. 275). Reports Isham 1991 p. 200: the CMC reduced Hamiltonian is time-dependent, implying energy enters or leaves, odd for the entire universe (p. 274).
assumptions: Defines Presentism as an objective spatially extended present (p. 261); Naturalism; SR-Realism.
conclusion: Monton's CMC route does not vindicate presentism; fixed-foliation QG breaks well-confirmed Lorentz symmetry; prospects of presentism are dim.
proof_status: Philosophical argument; technical CMC results cited from Isenberg 1995, Beig 1994, Rendall 1996.
dependencies: Monton 2006; Isham 1991; Isenberg 1995; Belot and Earman 2001.
limits: Predates Brading 2013/2015. Does not discuss dynamically individuated or system-relative presents, law-constitutive unity, or the universe's own present. Isham point is secondary report; Isham 1991 not read.
version: Petkov (ed.), Space, Time, and Spacetime, Fundamental Theories of Physics 167, Springer 2010, pp. 257-278; user-supplied PDF sha256 da293b2e1b8b9c1c3255512da41023751e28d51a4a0cd90aa87231ec78048b74
locator: pp. 260-261 (problem of time; Presentism definition), 263-264 (compatibilist strategies), 274 (Isham time-dependent Hamiltonian), 275 n. 21 (Monton emergent time)
open_questions: Does the Isham time-dependence point carry over from CMC to every global-time gauge for closed universes?

title: Presentism and Quantum Gravity
relevance: Origin of the presentism/quantum-gravity debate. Grants presentism is incompatible with SR and GR; argues fixed-foliation QG (CMC canonical QG, Bohmian QG) is compatible via a presentist theoretical hypothesis that one hypersurface of the foliation represents the existing events (preprint pp. 4-6). Dismisses relativized presentism as ad hoc (p. 6 n. 6). Claims presentism is a theory about time, not fundamental reality, so emergent time suffices (p. 20). Supplies the global-slice route for the universe (our horn 2a).
assumptions: Heraclitean presentism with a global three-dimensional present; scientific realism; QG supersedes GR.
conclusion: Presentism is compatible with our most fundamental physics 'for now', via fixed-foliation QG; M theory and loop QG appear incompatible.
dependencies: Beig 1994; Fischer and Moncrief 1997; Isenberg 1995; Kuchar 1992, 1999; Belot and Earman 2001; Callender 2000.
limits: Read the author's preprint dated 18 May 2005, not the published Dieks (2006) pagination (pp. 263-280); page locators are preprint pages. Predates Brading. No local, system-relative or dynamically individuated presents; no unity criterion; no discussion of the universe's conserved quantities or Isham's time-dependent Hamiltonian point.
version: Author preprint 'Presentism and Quantum Gravity', 18 May 2005, 26 pp.; user-supplied PDF sha256 0ca00b659bba36775cf21c99fd83658f5414aceaab6243f1c5e1a40039870c8b; published in Dieks (ed.), The Ontology of Spacetime, Elsevier 2006, 263-280
locator: preprint pp. 4-6 (fixed foliation and presentist theoretical hypothesis), p. 6 n. 6 (relativized presentism ad hoc), pp. 10-13 (Belot-Earman, Kuchar), p. 19 (CMC foliation depends on matter), p. 20 (presentism about time, not fundamental reality)
open_questions: Does Monton's fixed-foliation present for the universe satisfy a conservation-based unity criterion?
